evidence_items.supports: BASE requires executable async/concurrency/atomics semantics and compiler/runtime proof.
Current ClayCode already separates semantic hashes, epochs, capabilities and effect intent; no general CAS identity/memory-order record is present in the inspected V3 slice.
Async replay work separates semantic task/effect identity from physical scheduling and explicitly leaves conflicting accesses to synchronization/transaction semantics.
Earlier authority-budget experiments found atomic reservation necessary under concurrency/replay; this is adjacent shared-ancestry evidence, not independent proof of CAS semantics.

evidence_items.source: Rust standard library atomic Ordering / compare_exchange documentation
evidence_items.supports: Rust exposes explicit Relaxed/Acquire/Release/AcqRel/SeqCst ordering; compare_exchange uses separate success/failure ordering and documents ABA when equality is used as identity.

evidence_items.source: LLVM Language Reference and Atomic Instructions and Concurrency Guide
evidence_items.supports: LLVM cmpxchg is an atomic read-modify-write with explicit success/failure orderings; weak cmpxchg may fail spuriously; failure ordering has stricter constraints.
ECMAScript SharedArrayBuffer Atomics are sequentially consistent, showing that backend atomic ordering surfaces are not identical.
